translation:
The target consists of three definitions:

1. Def2 is a predicate on an arithmetic sentence σ (a closed formula of first-order arithmetic in the language ℒₒᵣ) asserting that σ is true in the standard model, the natural numbers (ℕ↓[ℒₒᵣ] ⊧ σ).

2. Def3 is a predicate on a set K of arithmetic sentences (K : Def1, where Def1 is Set ArithmeticSentence) asserting that for every sentence σ ∈ K, Def2 σ holds—that is, every sentence in K is true in the standard model of the natural numbers. No additional conditions (such as deductive closure or recursive enumerability) are required of K.

3. Def4 is a predicate on a set K of arithmetic sentences (K : Def1), viewed as an ArithmeticTheory (a set of axioms of the same type), asserting that K is consistent (Entailment.Consistent K)—that is, K does not prove a contradiction in classical first-order logic. Again, no other conditions are imposed on K.

divergences.description: Def2 and Def3 restrict truth (and thus soundness K ⊆ T) to first-order arithmetic sentences in the language ℒₒᵣ interpreted in the standard model ℕ, whereas [P-K351] introduces T informally as the set of sentences that are true without explicitly restricting to first-order arithmetic (though the author's claim itself specifies truth of an arithmetic sentence).

Def4 defines consistency specifically as classical first-order deductive consistency of a set of sentences in ℒₒᵣ (Entailment.Consistent K), whereas [P-K345] emphasizes generality across 'any sufficiently strong formal system', which need not be restricted to classical first-order theories in the language of arithmetic.

judgement.summary: The three definitions faithfully capture truth of a first-order arithmetic sentence in ℕ, soundness of K (K ⊆ T), and meta-level consistency, with only minor idealizations fixing the language to ℒₒᵣ and the deductive framework to classical first-order logic.
